title: Sell Mineral Rights in Eddy County, TX/NM
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Eddy County, NM | Royalty Buyer
metaDescription: Eddy County, New Mexico sits at the heart of the Delaware Basin's most active drilling. Get a candid cash offer from a former E&P operations engineer.
heroLead: If you had told me twenty years ago that Eddy County, New Mexico would become one of the hottest counties in the entire Permian, I'd have said you were thinking of the wrong state.
intro: Eddy County runs the New Mexico side of the Delaware Basin story, centered on Carlsbad and stretching out through Artesia and a string of smaller communities that grew up around potash mining before oil ever mattered much here. Today it's a different picture entirely, with Bone Spring and Wolfcamp horizontal drilling running at a pace that rivals anything happening on the Texas side of the line.

Because New Mexico's regulatory and royalty framework differs from Texas in some meaningful ways, mineral owners here sometimes get valuations from Texas-focused buyers that don't quite fit. I've worked both sides of the state line long enough to price an Eddy County interest correctly, and I'll walk you through what actually matters.

sections.heading: New Mexico's different rules matter for value
paragraphs: New Mexico state trust lands and federal BLM acreage make up a larger share of Eddy County than most Texas counties in this basin, and that affects both the pace of permitting and the royalty structure on a given unit. If your minerals sit under or near state or federal acreage, the surrounding development timeline can be different than a comparable tract just across the line in Texas.

New Mexico also handles spacing and pooling differently than Texas, and its statutory royalty rate on state leases can be higher than what you'd typically see negotiated privately. None of that changes the fundamentals of how I value your interest, but it's part of why I ask specifically which side of the state line and what kind of surface ownership sits above your minerals.

sections.heading: Carlsbad, Artesia, and the acreage between them
paragraphs: The corridor between Carlsbad and Artesia has seen some of the most concentrated horizontal drilling in the entire Delaware Basin over the past several years, with major public operators running dense multi-well pad programs across large acreage blocks. Interests in that corridor tend to have more current production data and more visible future development to underwrite against.

Smaller communities scattered through the rest of the county, places like Atoka and Happy Valley, sit closer to the edges of that core activity, which doesn't mean the minerals are worthless, it just means I lean more heavily on nearby permitting trends than on your current check alone when I build a range.

sections.heading: What builds a defensible offer
paragraphs: I look at net mineral acres, your specific decimal interest, the decline stage of producing wells, and permitted-but-undrilled locations nearby. Eddy County's active permitting pace means the third factor carries real weight here, since a well that hasn't spud yet can still meaningfully affect what a buyer is willing to pay for adjacent undeveloped minerals.

Values vary with commodity price and how close your tract sits to the current core development, so I won't quote a flat number on this page. What I will tell you is that a recent check stub or division order gets me to a real, specific range much faster than a guess based on the county name alone.

sections.heading: Potash, ranching, and split mineral ownership
paragraphs: A fair amount of Eddy County mineral ownership traces back through ranching families and, in some pockets, through old potash-era land dealings that predate the current oil boom entirely. That history means fractional and heir-split ownership is common, and I regularly buy a single heir's share without needing the whole family to agree.

This page isn't legal or tax advice, and for questions specific to New Mexico probate or estate handling, talk to an attorney licensed there. What I can offer is a direct, no-pressure conversation and a written cash offer based on the real production picture behind your interest.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my Eddy County minerals are under state trust land, federal BLM, or private surface?
faqs.answer: Yes, it affects permitting pace and sometimes the royalty terms on the underlying lease. I ask about this early so the offer reflects your actual situation rather than a generic county average.

faqs.question: Is Eddy County still seeing active new drilling?
faqs.answer: Yes, particularly in the corridor between Carlsbad and Artesia, where multiple major operators continue running multi-well pad programs in the Bone Spring and Wolfcamp. That activity level factors directly into how I price nearby undeveloped or lightly developed acreage.

faqs.question: I live outside New Mexico, does that complicate selling my Eddy County interest?
faqs.answer: No. Most of my Eddy County sellers live out of state or even out of the region. Closing happens by mail or overnight courier, and I handle the New Mexico-specific title requirements on my end.

faqs.question: How is a New Mexico royalty interest different from a Texas one in terms of what you'll pay?
faqs.answer: The core valuation drivers are the same, current production, decline, and nearby development, but New Mexico's mix of state, federal, and private acreage and its statutory royalty framework can shift the specifics. I price each interest on its own facts rather than applying a Texas template.
